r0.why: Carbonate minerals, calcite/dolomite, recrystallized by heat and pressure [1]; crystalline, usually unfoliated with exceptions [2]; from sedimentary carbonate rocks [16].

r1.why: Variable recrystallization [17], interlocking mosaic of carbonate crystals [18], protolith textures modified or destroyed [19]; nothing added.

r2.why: Pure silicate-poor protolith [20], impurities list as grains or layers [21], serpentine green from Mg-rich rock with silica [22], mobilized and recrystallized by heat and pressure [23].

r3.why: Prized since classical times [38]; softness, homogeneity, shatter resistance [39]; low refraction index, 12.7-38 mm, waxy lifelike look, human form [40].

r4.why: Geology vs stonemasonry meaning [3]; dimension stone trade usage incl. some non-calcitic rocks [42]; Tennessee marble is Holston Formation limestone [43].

r5.why: Outdoor marble damaged by acid rain via carbonation, sulfation, black-crust with its contents [24]; avoid vinegar and acidic solutions [25].
